problem: Find the imaginary part of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1-7\text{i} & 2-4\text{i} \\ 6\text{i} & -5\end{aligned}].$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Matrix
examples.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/9e1718bbf8790a9cc89d7cc1c6dd7879f8e222f348e5a9a56fec83a1b033250d.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/e99949f7e98aee85a040f698b15822927d7aabea1e688337d209c8e1d08850d6.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072897/assets/642f01152b6a1717300120241f788a24098413648cd70e8d0399629f11be2254.png) then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
examples.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & -5-7\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} & 5-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,d=5,e=-3$ and $h=-9.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=2 \cdot 5 + (-3) \cdot (-9) = 37.
$$

feedback.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} & 3-2\text{i} \\ 3-3\text{i} & 1-5\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{11}+{b}_{22}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} & 3-2\text{i} \\ 3-3\text{i} & 1-5\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{2+4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3-2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{3-3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1-5\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-4\text{i} & 3+2\text{i} \\ 3+3\text{i} & 1+5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{11}+{b}_{22}=(2-4\text{i})+(1+5\text{i})=3+\text{i}.$
